v: When the Sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices so they could go and anoint the body of Jesus.
And the Sabbath having passed, Mary Magdalene and Mary the {mother} of James and Salome bought spices so that, having come, they might anoint him.

When the Jewish day of rest was over, Salome, Mary from the town of Magdala, and Mary, who was the mother of James, purchased fragrant ointments. They planned to visit {Jesus’ grave} and pour the ointments on his body {to finish burying him properly}.
Very early on the first day of the week, just after sunrise, they went to the tomb.
And very early on the first of the week, they arrive at the tomb, the sun having come up. \*
At dawn on Sunday morning, the three women visited Jesus’ tomb. \*
They were asking one another, “Who will roll away the stone from the entrance of the tomb?
And they were saying to one another, “Who will roll away the stone for us from the door of the tomb?”
{As they were walking,} they asked each other, “Who will help us by rolling the flat stone to open the entrance to the grave?”
But when they looked up, they saw that the stone had been rolled away, even though it was extremely large.
And having looked up, they see that the stone has been rolled away, for it was extremely large. \*
{When they arrived,} they looked {at the grave} and noticed that someone had already rolled the flat stone {to open the entrance to the grave}. And that flat stone was huge! \*
When they entered the tomb, they saw a young man dressed in a white robe sitting on the right side, and they were alarmed.
And having entered into the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, dressed in a white robe, and they were alarmed.
Then, the three women walked into the grave, where they saw a young man. He was wearing a white robe and was sitting down to their right. What they saw startled them!
But he said to them, “Do not be alarmed. You are looking for Jesus the Nazarene, who was crucified. He has risen! He is not here! See the place where they put Him.
But he says to them, “Do not be alarmed. You seek Jesus, the Nazarene, the one having been crucified. He was raised up! He is not here. Behold, {this is} the place where they put him.

The young man told them, “Do not let what you see startle you! {I know that} you are looking for the body of Jesus from the town of Nazareth. He was the one whom soldiers killed by nailing him to a cross. God has made him alive again! He is no longer in this grave. Look at where people placed his body.

But go, tell His disciples and Peter, ‘He is going ahead of you into Galilee. There you will see Him, just as He told you.
But go, say to his disciples and to Peter, ‘He is going before you to Galilee. There you will see him, just as he said to you.’” \*

Now depart to his apprentices and tell them, especially Peter, that Jesus is going ahead of them to the region of Galilee. {Tell them that} Jesus will meet them there, which is what Jesus already told them.” \*
So the women left the tomb and ran away, trembling and bewildered. And in their fear they did not say a word to anyone.
And having gone out, they fled from the tomb, for trembling and amazement was gripping them. And they said nothing to anyone, for they were afraid. \*
The three women were shaking because what had happened amazed them. So they left the grave and ran away. Because they felt afraid, they did not speak to anyone {about what had happened}. \*
Early on the first day of the week, after Jesus had risen, He appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom He had driven out seven demons.
[Now having arisen early in the morning on the first of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven demons.
[When Jesus lived again early on Sunday morning, Mary from the town of Magdala was the first person to see him. Jesus had forced seven demons out of her.
She went and told those who had been with Him, who were mourning and weeping.
That {one}, going, reported {it} to the ones having been with him, mourning and weeping.
She approached Jesus’ apprentices, who were grieving very much. She told them {what she had seen}.
And when they heard that Jesus was alive and she had seen Him, they did not believe it.
And those {ones}, having heard that he lives and was seen by her, did not believe. \*
So, the apprentices learned that Jesus was alive and that Mary had seen him. However, they did not accept what she said. \*

After this, Jesus appeared in a different form to two of them as they walked along in the country.
Now after these things, he appeared in a different form to two of them walking, going into the country.
Sometime later, two of Jesus’ apprentices were traveling to farm areas. They saw Jesus, although he looked different.
And they went back and reported it to the rest, but they did not believe them either.
And those {ones}, having gone away, reported {it} to the rest, but they did not believe those {ones}. \*
Then, the two apprentices went back {to Jerusalem}. They told the other apprentices what had happened, but the others did not accept what the two apprentices said. \*
Later, as they were eating, Jesus appeared to the Eleven and rebuked them for their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they did not believe those who had seen Him after He had risen.

Now later, he appeared to the Eleven, they reclining to eat, and he rebuked their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they did not believe the ones having seen him, having been raised from the dead.

Sometime later, Jesus revealed himself to his 11 representatives while they were eating. Because they had not accepted it when people told them that they had seen Jesus after God made him alive again, Jesus scolded them. He told them that they should not have stubbornly refused to accept what those people said.

And he said to them, “Having gone into all the world, preach the gospel to all the creation.
Then he told them, “Visit every place and proclaim the good news to every person!
Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned.
The one having believed and having been baptized will be saved, but the one not having believed will be condemned. \*
God will rescue all people who trust in me and who have someone baptize them. However, God will punish all people who do not trust in me. \*

As for the apprentices, they left {Jerusalem} and proclaimed {the good news} in every place. The Lord {Jesus} helped them and enabled them to perform miracles. That way, people could see that the good news was true. May it be so!]
